newsitem.title: SYRIA: Syria wants army ready to confront Israeli plans.
newsitem.headline: Syria wants army ready to confront Israeli plans.

text.p: Syria's army chief of staff Hikmat Shihabi called on the military to be ready to confront Israeli forces, saying peace was not the only option for recovering the Golan Heights.

"Duties and responsibilities of our men in the armed forces are increasing in light of the current situation," Shihabi said in a graduation ceremony of military engineering officers on Wednesday night. His remarks were published in newspapers on Thursday.
"That requires us to redouble efforts...and keep a high degree of fighting readiness that would enable our forces to abort the Zionist (Israeli) plans aiming at killing the peace process.

"The recent aggressive step of the government of (Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin) Netanyahu to take the approval of the Knesset (parliament) to keep occupation of the Golan is a clear evidence of this arrogant policy that fills the region with tension, escalation and explosion," he said.

Shihabi last week warned of war after Netanyahu gave his support to a law that would make withdrawal from the Golan very hard, stipulating the approval of 80 members of the 120-seat Knesset for territorial concessions. Israel seized the Golan Heights in 1967.

"Peace is syria's startegic option but it should be just, comprehensive...This option did not come out of weakness or retreat, and if it is our startegic option that does not mean it is the only option we have to return lands and rights,"Shihabi said.

"We will return our occupied lands with all means and abilities we have, and our armed forces will be in the front line to return lands and rights," added Shihabi, who took part in peace talks in the United States Between Syria and Israel's former Labour government.
Official Syrian newspapers said on Thursday that Syria was not isolated in the region, pointing to President Hafez al-Assad's visit to Iran last week.

"Netanyahu's government thought that Syria was isolated, that the Turkish-Israeli alliance has tightend the isolation and that Syria would soon be forced to follow the path which this racist government has drawn for the countries of the region," the ruling party newspaper al-Baath said.
Al-baath said Assad's visit to Tehran "confirmed with no doubt or mystery the very strong strategic ties between Syria and Iran".

The official daily al-Thawra said an expected visit by U.S. envoy Dennis Ross to the Middle East would not be easy but might bear fruit if the United States pressured Netanyahu to change his policies.
"The American mission will not be easy and needs a lot of patience...and in the first place needs using pressures and bridling Netanyahu," it said.
"We are sure that Washington is capable of curbing this irresponsible man and if it followed the right and honest way it could return the peace process to its right track," it added.
